evaluation.final_reason: Initial substantive disagreement about whether the tissue packet legitimately held the table (Round 1) was resolved when all parties agreed to a compromise—finding another table—and A volunteered to search (Round 3). No substantive disputes reappeared in subsequent rounds.

round_scores.evidence: A asserts the tissue packet was left to hold the place (Turn 1); B says they saw the table as available and moved the packet (Turn 2); C criticizes moving someone else's packet (Turn 3). Clear substantive disagreement about whether the reservation should be respected.

Participants quickly agree on principles of respecting reservations and fairness and propose finding another table as a solution (Turns 5-8). Only very minor residual disagreement remains, as they converge on a compromise.

A accepts the compromise and volunteers to look for another table (Turn 9); B, C, and D express agreement and readiness to search (Turns 10-12). The substantive dispute is affirmatively resolved by consensus on the alternative.
All four participants continue cooperative table-searching with no signs of renewed disagreement (Turns 13-16).
